headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-mediated interaction: Roo Code can write shared workspace files while Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, and Roo Code can read/write VS Code workspace files and use browser screenshots. If Roo Code places attacker-controlled text into shared files or screenshots that Perplexity later consumes, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Roo Code writes untrusted content into a workspace file that Perplexity later uploads or reads
IF Perplexity treats file or browsing content as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable file upload from Perplexity for shared artifacts
Use a read-only export step before Perplexity review
Add a manual provenance check before copying content between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and handles model provider API keys, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context. If the same workspace contains secrets or sensitive code, Perplexity can ingest it through uploads or browsing artifacts. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so a shared-workspace leakage path exists in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace
IF those files are uploaded or copied into Perplexity for analysis
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Use redacted copies for Perplexity review
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive documents
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Perplexity has vendor-hosted browsing and can also access files it is given. Both can touch the same workspace-adjacent artifacts, and Roo Code explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. Without locking or coordination, concurrent edits and git-state races are dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent commits or rewrites files while the other is also editing
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Run a quick diff review before any commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG answer engine that produces cited outputs, while Roo Code can act on workspace files and git state. If Roo Code treats Perplexity’s answers as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. The pair does not document a verification gate, so the pathway exists in default workflows but is not automatically catastrophic.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Perplexity output as a direct implementation spec
IF no human or automated verification step checks the cited answer before code changes
mitigations: Require a second-source check before edits
Ask Roo Code to summarize assumptions separately
Review citations manually before committing
Limit Perplexity to research-only tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Roo Code handles source code and model provider API keys. If regulated or secret material is placed into Perplexity, it may flow into a vendor-hosted service; Roo Code’s workspace access can expose the same material locally. The profiles do not show matching compliance guarantees, so a retention/residency mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are copied into Perplexity
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency constraints
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity prompts
Use sanitized excerpts only
Confirm retention settings before upload
Document a data-handling boundary for the workspace
